title: Bessie Smith and hearing the blues in the South
summary: She heard the blues in the South, was compared to Bessie Smith, and says she learned from her in time.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: has meant something to you. Well, uh, in the South, in New Orleans where I was born, I didn't get a chance to hear, uh, the great singers like Roland Hayes and, and, um, uh, Grace Moore, Lily Pond, and all those great singers until I came to Chicago up north. Well, we, we did have a chance to hear the blues down there because it's the type of thing that you can hear in the South as soon as you get off the train. People in the South have the, uh, radios or the old-time phonograph just as loud and you can hear the blues. You know, the blues were born in the South and they don't mind playing them and they're not ashamed of it. Everybody, that's one thing that people in the South love the blues and they play it. In fact, all of America loves the blues. And of course, we, um, we got a chance to, uh, to hear more of Bessie Smith. And I suppose basically, uh, that's why so many people say that, uh, I sound like Bessie Smith, but, uh, I suppose I do. She, she was a great singer. It's an honor to sound like her. But, uh, I don't think I sound as great as Bessie. But there, since she's dead, they're giving me the credit that, uh, this is the living Bessie Smith.
But you wouldn't say that you have learned, uh, directly from listening to her. No, no, because

time has advanced so fast. I've had, I've lived up north here for more than 25 years. Now I've had a chance to hear the best of singers and, uh, uh, and to listen to them on radio and television and that the great concerts hold here. Well, I, uh, I, uh, I, uh, I have, I have heard some of the finest artists. But I still think Bessie is a, is a great artist. But I have learned a lot from her time.
